\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مخلص} (mukhlis)}{مخلص (mukhlis)}]{\ur{مخلص} (mukhlis) — sincere}

\label{lesson:UR-C457-mukhlis}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for grace, then the Urdu for cruelty.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مخلص}}
\textbf{\ur{مخلص}} — \emph{mukhlis} — \textquotedblleft{}sincere\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{وہ} \ur{ایک} \ur{مخلص} \ur{دوست} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{voh ek mukhlis dost hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He is a sincere friend.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مخلص}} (\emph{mukhlis}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{mukhliṣ}, \textquotedblleft{}sincere, devoted\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mukhlis}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{voh ek mukhlis dost hai.} — He is a sincere friend.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for grace, then the Urdu for cruelty, then say \emph{mukhlis} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اعتبار} \ur{کرنا} (etibār karnā)}{اعتبار کرنا (etibār karnā)}]{\ur{اعتبار} \ur{کرنا} (etibār karnā) — to believe someone; to trust their word}

\label{lesson:UR-C457-etibar-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for sincere, then the Urdu for crafty.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اعتبار} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{اعتبار} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{etibār karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to believe someone; to trust their word\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{میں} \ur{نے} \ur{اس} \ur{کی} \ur{بات} \ur{کا} \ur{اعتبار} \ur{کیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maiṅ ne us kī bāt kā etibār kiyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I took him at his word.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{دوست} \ur{کا} \ur{اعتبار} \ur{کیا}, \emph{us ne dost kā etibār kiyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اعتبار} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{etibār karnā}) is built from \textbf{\ur{اعتبار}}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{iʿtibār}, \textquotedblleft{}regard, credit\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{کرنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{etibār karnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maiṅ ne us kī bāt kā etibār kiyā.} — I took him at his word.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for sincere, then the Urdu for crafty, then say \emph{etibār karnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{دیانت} (diyānat)}{دیانت (diyānat)}]{\ur{دیانت} (diyānat) — honesty; integrity}

\label{lesson:UR-C457-diyanat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for crafty, then the Urdu for to believe someone.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{دیانت}}
\textbf{\ur{دیانت}} — \emph{diyānat} — \textquotedblleft{}honesty; integrity\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دکاندار} \ur{کی} \ur{دیانت} \ur{پر} \ur{سب} \ur{کو} \ur{بھروسا} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dukāndār kī diyānat par sab ko bharosā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

Feminine.

\textbf{\ur{دیانت}} (\emph{diyānat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{diyāna}, \textquotedblleft{}religion, uprightness\textquotedblright{}.
